taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: NTLM service binding, signing and relay-resistance configuration
controls.source_trace: Identify an actual trusted-authentication relay path and target binding requirements from configuration. Keep credential coercion/relay execution outside ordinary review.
controls.implementation_branch: Branch by receiving protocol: signing, extended protection/channel binding and service configuration are not interchangeable defenses. The absence of one setting does not prove a relay chain without an available authentication source and accepted destination. Use configuration and owned protocol fixtures; do not coerce production users or collect NTLM exchanges.
controls.operational_method: Build a receiving-protocol matrix for the actual path: SMB signing, LDAP signing/channel binding and HTTP extended protection/TLS termination are different checks. Record server enforcement, client support and whether a proxy terminates or forwards the authenticated channel. An absent setting is a lead until a feasible source/destination and accepted operation are shown. Use configuration and isolated owned fixtures; no production authentication coercion or relay is required.
controls.controlled_verification: Use only an owned isolated authentication fixture or supplied configuration evidence to compare enforced and absent target binding.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: NTLM enabled or signing optional at one host is not proof of an exploitable relay chain with a suitable source and target.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Enforce appropriate channel/service binding or remove the unnecessary path, verifying supported legitimate clients.
